title: Monitoring and assessment of lysosomal membrane damage in cultured cells using the high-content imager
protocol: Place sterile coverslips into a 6-well plate (5 coverslips/well).
Coat the coverslips with Cellmatrix Type I-C diluted 10 times with sterile water.
Incubate the plate for at least 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the coverslips with PBS twice.
Plate cells onto the coverslips (1.0–2.0×10^5 cells/well).
Optimize the cell number for your experimental setup.
Ensure cells are at 70%–80% confluency the next day.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO₂ for 18–24 hours at 37°C.
Add 2 mL of LLOMe containing culture medium at a final concentration of 1 mM.
Incubate the cells for 1 hour at 37°C.
Remove the LLOMe solution and wash the cells gently with 2 mL of PBS twice.
Add 2 mL of fresh culture medium.
Incubate the cells for 1 or 10 hours at 37°C.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of PBS twice.
Remove PBS, add 1 mL of 4% PFA and incubate the cells for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C under aluminum foil.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of PBS twice.
Permeabilize the cells with 50 μg/mL digitonin-PBS solution for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS twice.
Incubate the cells with 0.2% gelatin-PBS for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C to block non-specific binding sites.
Wash the samples with PBS twice.
Incubate the cells with 40 μL/coverslip of anti-Galectin-3 primary antibody solution diluted at a ratio of 1:1,000 in 0.2% gelatin-PBS for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate the samples at 4°C for 14–18 h.
Wash the samples with PBS for 5 min three times.
Incubate the cells with 40 μL/coverslip of the secondary antibody solution diluted at 1:500 with 0.2% gelatin-PBS solution for 40–60 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS for 5 min three times.
Drop 5–10 μL/coverslip of the mounting medium with DAPI onto glass slides and mount the coverslips at cell surface-down.
Remove the excess mounting medium with filter papers and seal the coverslips with nail polish.
Plate PlatE cells at 2.0 × 10^6 cell/dish in a 6 cm dish with culture medium.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 18–24 h at 37°C.
Mix 3 μg of pMRX_IRES-puro_GFP-Gal3 and 3 μg of pVSVG in 250 μL of OPTI-MEM.
Add 16 μL of PEI to 250 μL of OPTI-MEM and mix well.
Mix tube-1 and tube-2 and incubate for 15 min at 20°C–25°C.
Drop 500 μL of the mixture into 2.5 mL fresh culture medium.
Gently shake the dish to mix.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 24 h at 37°C.
Change to fresh culture medium and incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 24 h at 37°C.
Plate HeLa cells at 1.0 × 10^5 cells/well in a 6-well plate one day before infection.
At 48 h post-transfection, filter the culture medium with a sterilized 0.45 μm PVDF filter to remove cell debris.
Mix 200–500 μL of virus-containing medium with 2 μL of 4 mg/mL polybrene.
Drop the mixture into 2 mL of fresh culture medium in the 6-well plate.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 at 37°C for 14–18 h.
Replace to medium containing 3 μg/mL of puromycin.
Incubate and select the cells.
Add 100 μL of culture medium into each well of a 96-well glass bottom plate.
Plate 100 μL of cell suspension at 4,000 cells/100 μL in a 96 well-plate.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 18–24 hours.
Remove the medium from the cells.
Wash the cells with 200 μL of PBS twice.
Add 100 μL of LLOMe containing culture medium at a final concentration of 1 mM.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Remove the medium and wash the cells again with 200 μL of PBS gently.
Add 200 μL of fresh medium to the cells.
Incubate the cells for either 1 or 10 hours at 37°C.
Wash cells with 200 μL of PBS twice.
Remove PBS, add 100 μL of 4% PFA and incubate at 20°C–25°C under aluminum foil for 20 minutes.
Remove 4% PFA and wash the cells with 200 μL of PBS twice.
Add 100 μL of DAPI solution diluted at 1:2,000 with PBS and incubate at 20°C–25°C under aluminum foil for 30 minutes.
Remove DAPI solution and wash the cells with 200 μL of PBS twice.
Set the glass slides or 96 well-plate to the sample holder in CellVoyager CQ1.
Open the software “CQ1 Measurement”.
Select a saving folder using the “Save Setting” tab.
Choose wavelengths for imaging.
Adjust focus using the “Search” button, and manually fine-tune if necessary.
Set photographing areas as required.
Start capturing images by pressing the “Rec” button.
Open “CellPathfinder” software for image analysis.
Load the image datasets acquired from step 7 into CellPathfinder.
Set "Channels" you used in step 7.
Set "Object" to be recognized.
Set parameters to recognize the nuclei from DAPI signals.
Set parameters to recognize the cytoplasm.
Determine the Analysis Range.
Click “Feature” and select the datasets such as Size and Count.
Start the analysis with the “Start” button.
Export data as “CSV”.
Open the data file acquired in step 8.
Copy "WellID", "[Cell1] Count", "[Cell1] (Cytoplasm) Area (AVG)", and "[Cell1] (Gal3 (Cytoplasm)) Area TOTAL (AVG)" to an Excel sheet.
Divide [Cell1] (Gal3 (Cytoplasm)) Area TOTAL (AVG) by [Cell1] (Cytoplasm) Area (AVG).
Calculate the average of values from each well for 1 h-samples.
Divide the values from 10 h-samples by the average score from 1 h-samples.
Make a graph showing the Gal3-positive area per cell.
Test significant differences with GraphPad Prism.
